newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa chief downplays risk of German price war.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa chief downplays risk of German price war.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG chief executive Juergen Weber on Saturday said he did not expect a major air fares price war in Germany once European air travel is fully liberalised on April 1.
The Sueddeutsche Zeitung cited Weber as saying it would be impossible to undercut Lufthansa significantly on its major routes and still turn a profit.
British Airways' German subsidiary would have gone under long ago without the hundreds of millions of marks in subsidies it received from its parent, Weber alleged.

Deutsche British Airways had already almost exhausted a 340 million mark guarantee from BA, Weber said. The British airline would have to decide whether to increase its financial support or to "let prudence prevail."

Weber also said he was satisfied with Lufthansa's pre-tax profit of some 680 million marks in 1996, down around ten percent from the previous year, but said the carrier was aiming to raise that figure to one billion marks.
Lufthansa is to detail its full 1996 earnings in May.
Looking ahead, Weber said German air business was likely to decline but predicted three to five percent annual growth in Europe and six to eight percent growth in inter-continental business.
The future, he said, would not be characterised by competition between individual companies but rather by alliances between airlines.
Lufthansa planned to extend its own network of alliances, after existing agreements with United Airlines, SAS, Air Canada and others had helped reduce its costs and boost earnings.
The German airline needed in particular to expand in Asia, Weber said.
He would not comment on rumoured talks with Hong Kong's Cathay Pacific, but said agreements for this region should be struck by the end of this year.
